What Waiting Can Cost a Property Manager

An unready exterior can complicate a showing or an inspection when your calendar is already tight. If work delays the date a vacant unit can be marketed or occupied, the owner may face more uncollected rent. A rough way to discuss that exposure is to divide the monthly rent by 30. That is an estimate of daily rent, not a prediction of leasing time or net income.

Occupied properties have costs too. Overgrown beds and debris can prompt tenant complaints or run afoul of local maintenance rules or HOA requirements, potentially leading to notices or fines. Rules and penalties vary, so check each address instead of assuming every property has the same deadline.

Thick, wet leaves can shade turf and leave walkways messy. Debris near surface drains can interfere with water flow, while piles of leaves and brush can give pests a place to shelter. A recurring complaint or a poor first impression may also make it harder to keep a good tenant happy. The practical fix is to catch small problems before they become another work order.
Our Fall Cleanup Process for Rental Properties
A good cleanup starts with a written scope, not a vague promise to make the yard look better. Depending on the property and your quote, the work can include:

items: **Confirm the scope and access.** Share addresses, showing dates, priorities, access instructions, and any owner requirements. We identify what needs attention and document the starting condition.
**Remove leaves and debris.** Clear built-up leaves, fallen branches, and ordinary yard debris from agreed lawn and common areas.
**Clean the beds and refresh mulch.** Remove weeds and debris from landscape beds. Add mulch where it is included in the approved scope.
**Edge and trim.** Tidy lawn edges, borders, and growth around the entry and other high-visibility areas.
**Prune accessible shrubs.** Trim agreed shrubs and low growth that obstruct walkways, signs, or the view of the property. Specialized tree work is a separate discussion.
**Clear ground-level drainage areas and walkways.** Remove surface debris around accessible drains, paths, and entrances so they are easier to inspect and use.
**Haul off and document.** Remove the agreed debris, complete a final walkthrough, and provide before-and-after photos of the work.

Central Texas Fall Lawn and Freeze-Prep Advice
Plan Around Fall Weather and Dormant Grass

September through November is a useful planning window around Austin, but heat, rain, and leaf drop do not follow the same calendar every year. Schedule an initial cleanup, then check again after heavier leaf drop. Bermuda, zoysia, and St. Augustine are warm-season grasses: they slow down as temperatures fall and may turn brown during dormancy. Brown winter turf is not automatically a dead lawn, and extra watering is not a cure for normal dormancy. Follow local watering rules and the needs of the site.
Decide Whether Overseeding Makes Sense

Some owners choose cool-season ryegrass for winter color; others prefer to let the existing lawn rest. Overseeding adds watering and mowing needs, and the winter grass can compete with warm-season turf when spring arrives. Review the grass type, property use, water rules, and budget before adding seed. [Texas A&M AgriLife guidance](https://bexar-tx.tamu.edu/homehort/archives-of-weekly-articles-davids-plant-of-the-week/winter-ryegrass/) explains why the spring transition deserves attention.
Time Pre-Emergent for Winter Weeds

Pre-emergent treatments are intended to control targeted annual weeds before they emerge, not remove weeds already growing. Timing depends on the weed, weather, product, and lawn; late summer or early fall may be appropriate for some winter weeds. Some products can also prevent new grass seed from establishing. Coordinate any treatment with overseeding, follow the label, and use a qualified applicator as required. See [Texas A&M lawn management guidance](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/landscaping/bermudagrass-home-lawn-management-calendar/). Treatments are separate from cleanup unless specifically included in your quote.
Prepare Irrigation and Outdoor Faucets for a Freeze

Before freezing weather, disconnect hoses, protect exposed outdoor faucets, and plan for irrigation shutdown and drainage. Austin Water recommends turning off and draining automatic sprinkler systems for freezing weather. See its [cold-weather checklist](https://www.austintexas.gov/water/austin-water-cold-weather-tips). Systems differ, so coordinate system-specific work and backflow protection with an appropriate irrigation professional. Confirm this work separately; it is not automatically part of a yard cleanup.
